title: Progressive snapshot prefetch + hedged pagination for usage-stream queries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Recent tenant growth has increased tail latency on the Console's usage analytics endpoints (top-entities and timeseries explorers). Long scrolls/pagination with sparse temporal filters cause many cold reads from object storage and wide fanout to microshards, producing 95th/99th latency spikes and increased egress costs.

Proposed solution: Implement a progressive snapshot prefetch layer combined with hedged read pagination. Key ideas: (1) take short-lived, lightweight materialized snapshots of hot query slices (progressive snapshots) that are incrementally refreshed; (2) on client page requests, trigger an aggressive in-memory prefetch of the next N cursors while simultaneously issuing a hedged read to a second replica if the primary latency exceeds a small threshold; (3) attach a cheap probabilistic filter (tenant-local bloom) to avoid prefetching widely for low-selectivity queries; (4) provide per-tenant budget constraints and backpressure signals to avoid prefetch storms.

Why this is different: existing approaches focus on static prefix caching or increasing index density. Progressive snapshots avoid full materialization cost by capturing only the compact summary (indexed pointers + aggregate summaries) and allow the runtime to hydrate rows on demand with a prioritized queue. Hedged pagination reduces long-tail by trading small extra read load for large latency wins.

Implementation highlights:
- Add a SnapshotCoordinator microservice (new, lightweight, horizontally sharded by tenant group) that maintains snapshot metadata and refresh schedules. Snapshots are stored as small protobuf blobs in Redis with TTL and a signed version id.
- Prefetch worker within the QueryBroker that uses tenant-level budget tokens to schedule hydrating reads; worker uses a prioritized queue ordering by query recency and predicted access probability.
- Hedged read client: simple configurable policy (hedge-after-ms, max-hedges-per-request) which falls back to secondary region or a cold replica.\n- Sampling/metrics: add per-request tags that record prefetch hits/misses, hedged-read fired, and snapshot-staleness at time of read. Surface these in Console telemetry dashboards and in the rollout gate.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Extra memory/IO from prefetches vs latency benefits — mitigate with tenant budgets and probabilistic filters.
- Snapshot freshness: refresh frequency tuned by access pattern heuristics; stale-but-fast may be acceptable for dashboard UX.
- Complexity: adds a lightweight coordinator and more moving parts; keep APIs simple and observable.

Design artifacts: design doc draft: https://redwood-internal.docs/designs/progressive-snapshots (internal). Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5921 (WIP). Observability dashboard (perf-testing): https://grafana.redwood.io/d/usage-proto/hedge-prefetch-v0

Acceptance criteria:
- 95th latency for long-scroll usage queries reduced by >=40% in staged perf test (synthetic heavy tenants).
- Prefetch budget prevents >10% extra read IO on average across tenants during steady state (measured in perf run).
- Clear telemetry for snapshot hit rate, hedged-read rate, and budget throttles displayed in staging console.
- Backout toggle (runtime flag) with zero-downtime capability.
